## Import data

```{r}
read.csv(file = "data/penguin_dataset.csv" )
penguins <- read.csv(file = "data/penguin_dataset.csv" )

## Data visulatisation 
ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = bill_len,
                     y = bill_dep)) +
  labs(title = "Bill length and depth in penguins",
       x = "Bill length (mm)",
       y = "Bill depth (mm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_point()

## Refining the legends
ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = bill_len,
                     y = bill_dep,
                     colour = species)) +
    labs(title = "Bill length and depth in penguins",
       x = "Bill length (mm)",
       y = "Bill depth (mm)",
       colour = "Species") +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_point()

## Finer conntrol
ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = bill_len,
                     y = bill_dep,
                     colour = species)) +
    labs(title = "Bill length and depth in penguins",
       x = "Bill length (mm)",
       y = "Bill depth (mm)",
       colour = "Species") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")) +
  geom_point(size = 3,
             alpha = 0.6)
             
ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = bill_len,
                     y = bill_dep,
                     colour = body_mass,
                     shape = species)) +
    labs(title = "Bill length and depth in penguins",
       x = "Bill length (mm)",
       y = "Bill depth (mm)",
       colour = "body_mass") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")) +
  geom_point(size = 3,
             alpha = 0.6,)

## Storing plaot infromations (making objects)

p_flipper_len <- ggplot(data = penguins,
       mapping = aes(x = species,
                     y = flipper_len)) +
    labs(title = "Flipper length of penguins",
       x = "Species",
       y = "Flipper length (mm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_flipper_len +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0) +
  geom_jitter(size = 3,
              width = 0.25,
              alpha = 0.5)
## oultier aplha 0 sets outliers to transparent 
```


```{r}
p_flipper_len +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0) +
  geom_jitter(mapping = aes(colour = species),
              size = 3,
              width = 0.25,
              alpha = 0.5)
```
## Facets and combining plots

```{r}
p_bm_fl <- ggplot(data = penguins,
                  mapping = aes(x = body_mass,
                                y = flipper_len,
                                colour = species))
p_bm_fl +
  geom_point(size = 2,
             alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ island)

p_bm_fl +
  geom_point(size = 2,
             alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(sex ~ island)   
```
## Combining Plots and Patchwork

```{r}
p1 <- ggplot(penguins,
              aes(x = bill_dep,
                  y = bill_len,
                  colour = species)) +
      geom_point() +
      labs(title = "Flipper length and depth",
           x = "Bill depth (mm)",
           y = "Bill length (mm)")

p2 <- p_bm_fl +
      labs(title = "Body mass and flipper length",
           x = "Flipper length (mm)",
           y = "Body mass (g)") +
      geom_point() 
## One can use arithmetic operations over pathchwork  
```

## Generating some example data for eg. Heatmap generation

```{r}
set.seed(0982)
month_data <- tibble(
  date = seq(as.Date("2024-12-01"), 
              as.Date("2024-12-31"), 
              by = "day"),
  count = sample(1:20, 31, replace = TRUE)  # Random counts per day
) |>
  mutate(
    wday = wday(date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),  # Day of the week (Sun-Sat)
    week = (day(date) - 1) %/% 7 + 1  # Week number (1 to 5)
  )

month_data |> head()

ggplot(data = month_data,
       mapping = aes(x = week, 
                      y = wday, 
                      fill = count)) +
  geom_tile()

ggplot(data = month_data,
       mapping = aes(x = wday, 
                      y = week, 
                      fill = count)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "Month data",
           x = "Wday",
           y = "Week",
           fill = "Count")

```
## Line Plots and understanding trends

```{r}
set.seed(02) # Please set this seed for this example

# Create stock price data for three different stocks
dates <- seq.Date(from = as.Date("2024-01-01"), 
                  by = "week", 
                  length.out = 200)

stocks <- tibble(
  date = rep(dates, times = 3),
  stock = rep(c("Stock A", "Stock B", "Stock C"), each = length(dates)),
  price = c(
    100 + cumsum(rnorm(length(dates), mean = 0, sd = 5)),  # Stock A fluctuates around 100
    80 + cumsum(rnorm(length(dates), mean = 0, sd = 4)),   # Stock B fluctuates around 80
    120 + cumsum(rnorm(length(dates), mean = 0, sd = 6))   # Stock C fluctuates around 120
  )
)

ggplot(stocks |>  filter(stock == "Stock C"), 
        aes(x = date, 
            y = price)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Stock C Price Over Time", 
        x = "Date", 
        y = "Price") +
  theme_minimal()

## combining geom-line ad geom fill, AUC graphs, stacked area chart

ggplot(stocks  |>  filter(stock == "Stock B"), 
        aes(x = date, y = price)) +
  geom_area(fill = "black", 
            alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(color = "black", 
            linewidth = 0.5) +  # Keeps the line for clarity
  labs(title = "Stock B Price Over Time (Area Chart)", 
        x = "Date", 
        y = "Price") +
  theme_minimal()

## Stacked chart
ggplot(stocks, aes(x = date, 
                    y = price, 
                    fill = stock)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.6) +  # Fill areas with transparency
  labs(title = "Stacked Area Chart of Stock Prices Over Time",
       x = "Date", 
       y = "Price", 
       fill = "Stock") +
  theme_minimal()

```
## A proper holistic exercise

```{r}
parfumo_data_clean <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-12-10/parfumo_data_clean.csv')

parfumo_data_clean |> summary()
parfumo_data_clean |> glimpse()

##quick way to see would be to do a quick check on average means

parfumo_data_clean |> 
  group_by(Brand) |> 
  summarize(avg_Rating = mean(Rating_Value, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  arrange(desc(avg_Rating)) |> 
  head()

ggplot(data = parfumo_data_clean, 
      mapping = aes(x = Rating_Count, 
                    y = Rating_Value)) +
  geom_point()


ggplot(data = parfumo_data_clean, 
        mapping = aes(x = Release_Year, y = Rating_Count)) +
  geom_point()


```
